meta.source: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (Commonwealth of Australia 2020), testable Parts 1-4
meta.license_note: Questions are original. Facts are from the CC BY 4.0 resource book.
meta.rules: 20 questions, 5 values, pass = 5/5 values AND 15/20 overall, 45 minutes

questions.question: When did the First Fleet arrive from Great Britain?
questions.explain_en: The First Fleet of 11 convict ships arrived on 26 January 1788.
questions.explain_vi: Đoàn First Fleet gồm 11 tàu tù nhân đến ngày 26/01/1788.

questions.question: Who was the first Governor of the colony of New South Wales?
questions.explain_en: Captain Arthur Phillip was the first Governor of NSW.
questions.explain_vi: Thuyền trưởng Arthur Phillip là Thống đốc đầu tiên của NSW.

questions.question: What is Australia’s national language?
questions.explain_en: English is Australia’s national language and part of our national identity.
questions.explain_vi: Tiếng Anh là quốc ngữ của Úc.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Australia?
questions.explain_en: Canberra, in the ACT, is Australia’s capital city.
questions.explain_vi: Canberra (ACT) là thủ đô nước Úc.

questions.question: On which date is Australia Day celebrated?
questions.explain_en: Australia Day is 26 January, the anniversary of the First Fleet’s arrival.
questions.explain_vi: Ngày Quốc khánh Úc là 26/01, kỷ niệm First Fleet đến Úc.

questions.question: What is Australia’s system of government?
questions.explain_en: Australia is a parliamentary democracy. Power comes from the people through elections.
questions.explain_vi: Úc là nền dân chủ đại nghị. Quyền lực đến từ nhân dân qua bầu cử.

questions.question: What does the Rule of Law mean in Australia?

options.text: Religious rules are above the law
Only ordinary people must obey the law
No person or group is above the law

questions.explain_en: Everyone, including leaders and police, must obey Australian laws.
questions.explain_vi: Không ai, kể cả lãnh đạo và cảnh sát, đứng trên pháp luật.

questions.question: Which of these is a responsibility of Australian citizens?

options.text: Serve in the Defence Force as a full-time job

questions.explain_en: Citizens must obey Australian laws. ADF service is voluntary.
questions.explain_vi: Công dân phải tuân thủ luật pháp. Phục vụ quân đội là tự nguyện.

questions.question: From what age must Australian citizens vote in federal elections?
questions.explain_en: Voting is a responsibility for citizens aged 18 years or over.
questions.explain_vi: Công dân từ 18 tuổi trở lên có nghĩa vụ đi bầu.

questions.question: Which of these is a privilege of Australian citizenship?

options.text: Ignore Australian laws if you have another citizenship

questions.explain_en: Citizens may apply for an Australian passport and re-enter Australia freely.
questions.explain_vi: Công dân được xin hộ chiếu Úc và nhập cảnh lại tự do.

questions.question: When did the colonies unite to form the Commonwealth of Australia?
questions.explain_en: Federation was on 1 January 1901.
questions.explain_vi: Liên bang được thành lập ngày 01/01/1901.

questions.question: Who is Australia’s Head of State?
questions.explain_en: The Head of State is the King of Australia, His Majesty King Charles III.
questions.explain_vi: Nguyên thủ Quốc gia là Quốc vương Úc, Đức vua Charles III.

questions.question: Who is the leader of the Australian Government?
questions.explain_en: The Prime Minister is the leader of the Australian Government.
questions.explain_vi: Thủ tướng là người lãnh đạo Chính phủ Úc.

questions.question: What is the other name sometimes used for the House of Representatives?
questions.explain_en: The House of Representatives is also called the Lower House or the People’s House.
questions.explain_vi: Hạ viện còn gọi là Viện dân biểu (People’s House).

questions.question: Which level of government is responsible for immigration and citizenship?
questions.explain_en: Immigration and citizenship are federal responsibilities.
questions.explain_vi: Nhập cư và quốc tịch thuộc chính phủ liên bang.

questions.question: Under the Rule of Law, who must obey Australian laws?

options.text: Only people who were born in Australia
Everyone in Australia, including people in power
Only people who are not religious

questions.explain_en: Australian laws apply to all people in Australia. No person or group is above the law.
questions.explain_vi: Luật Úc áp dụng cho mọi người ở Úc. Không ai đứng trên pháp luật.

questions.question: Does Australia have an official national religion?

options.text: Yes, whatever religion the Prime Minister follows
No. People are free to follow any religion or none

questions.explain_en: Australia has no official national religion. The government is secular.
questions.explain_vi: Úc không có quốc giáo. Chính phủ là thế tục.

questions.question: Is it against the law to discriminate against a person because of their gender?

options.text: No, employers may choose any rule they like
Yes. Men and women have equal rights

questions.explain_en: Men and women have equal rights. Gender discrimination is against the law.
questions.explain_vi: Nam nữ bình đẳng. Kỳ thị vì giới tính là trái luật.

questions.question: What does a ‘fair go’ mean in Australia?

options.text: People succeed because of wealth or family background
What someone achieves should come from their talents, work and effort
Jobs must be given to the oldest applicant

questions.explain_en: A fair go means success should come from talent and effort, not wealth or background.
questions.explain_vi: ‘Fair go’ nghĩa là thành quả nhờ tài năng và nỗ lực, không phải giàu có hay gốc gác.

questions.question: Is domestic and family violence against the law in Australia?

options.text: No, it is a private family matter
Only if the couple is not married
Yes. It is a serious crime for men and women

questions.explain_en: Domestic and family violence is illegal, including in the home and in marriage.
questions.explain_vi: Bạo lực gia đình là tội nghiêm trọng, kể cả trong nhà và trong hôn nhân.

questions.question: How many ships were in the First Fleet?
questions.explain_en: The First Fleet was 11 convict ships.
questions.explain_vi: First Fleet gồm 11 tàu tù nhân.

questions.question: When did the gold rush begin in New South Wales and Victoria?
questions.explain_en: Gold was discovered in NSW and Victoria in 1851.
questions.explain_vi: Thời kỳ cơn sốt Vàng bắt đầu khi vàng được phát hiện ở NSW và Victoria năm 1851.

questions.question: What is the capital city of New South Wales?
questions.explain_en: Sydney is the capital of NSW and Australia’s largest city.
questions.explain_vi: Sydney là thủ phủ NSW và thành phố lớn nhất nước Úc.

questions.question: What is Australia’s national flower?
questions.explain_en: The golden wattle is Australia’s national flower.
questions.explain_vi: Hoa keo vàng (golden wattle) là quốc hoa Úc.

questions.question: What is Australia’s national anthem?
questions.explain_en: The national anthem is Advance Australia Fair.
questions.explain_vi: Quốc ca là Advance Australia Fair (Nước Úc tiến bước hùng cường).

questions.question: How do Australians believe change should happen?

options.text: Through discussion, peaceful persuasion and the democratic process

questions.explain_en: Australians reject violence as a way to change a person’s mind or the law.
questions.explain_vi: Người Úc tin thay đổi phải qua bàn thảo, thuyết phục ôn hòa và dân chủ.

questions.question: What does freedom of association mean?

options.text: You must join a political party
You may join a legal organisation, or decide not to join
Only citizens may meet in public

questions.explain_en: People are free to join or not join a legal group and cannot be forced.
questions.explain_vi: Được tự do gia nhập hoặc không gia nhập tổ chức hợp pháp; không bị ép buộc.

questions.question: Which of these is a responsibility of Australian citizens aged 18 or over?

options.text: Serve on a jury if called to do so

questions.explain_en: Jury service, if requested, is a responsibility for citizens 18+ on the electoral roll.
questions.explain_vi: Bồi thẩm đoàn (nếu được gọi) là nghĩa vụ của công dân từ 18 tuổi.

questions.question: Can Australian citizens apply for children born overseas to become citizens by descent?

options.text: Yes, this is a privilege of citizenship
Only if the child has never visited Australia

questions.explain_en: Citizens can apply for a child born overseas to become a citizen by descent.
questions.explain_vi: Công dân có thể đăng ký quốc tịch theo huyết thống cho con sinh ở nước ngoài.

questions.question: Who collects income tax in Australia?
questions.explain_en: Tax on money you earn is collected by the ATO.
questions.explain_vi: Thuế thu nhập do Sở Thuế vụ Úc (ATO) thu.

questions.question: What is the Australian Constitution?

options.text: A speech by the Prime Minister
The legal document that sets out the basic rules for the government of Australia
The rules of the Australian Labor Party

questions.explain_en: The Constitution is the supreme legal document for Australia’s government.
questions.explain_vi: Hiến pháp là văn bản pháp lý nêu các quy định cơ bản cho chính phủ Úc.

questions.question: How can the Australian Constitution be changed?

options.text: By a decision of the Prime Minister alone
By a vote in a referendum
By the High Court issuing a new flag

questions.explain_en: The people change the Constitution by voting in a referendum.
questions.explain_vi: Người dân thay đổi Hiến pháp bằng trưng cầu dân ý.

questions.question: How many senators does each Australian state elect?
questions.explain_en: Each state elects 12 senators, regardless of size or population.
questions.explain_vi: Mỗi tiểu bang bầu 12 thượng nghị sĩ, không phụ thuộc dân số.

questions.question: What is the leader of a state government called?
questions.explain_en: The leader of a state government is the Premier. Territory leaders are Chief Ministers.
questions.explain_vi: Lãnh đạo chính phủ tiểu bang là Thủ hiến (Premier).

questions.question: Which level of government is usually responsible for hospitals and schools?
questions.explain_en: Hospitals, schools, police and public transport are primarily state and territory responsibilities.
questions.explain_vi: Bệnh viện, trường học chủ yếu thuộc tiểu bang và lãnh thổ.

questions.question: Is voting compulsory in Australian federal elections?

options.text: Yes. This shows the importance of taking part in elections
Only for people born in Australia

questions.explain_en: Voting is compulsory in Australia for federal and state or territory elections.
questions.explain_vi: Bỏ phiếu là bắt buộc ở Úc trong bầu cử liên bang và tiểu bang/lãnh thổ.

questions.question: People in Australia may protest against the government if the protest is:
questions.explain_en: Peaceful public protest is part of democracy. It must not injure people or damage property.
questions.explain_vi: Biểu tình ôn hòa, đúng luật là một phần của dân chủ.

questions.question: If an Australian law conflicts with a religious practice, which one prevails?
questions.explain_en: Where there is a conflict, Australian law prevails. Religious laws have no legal status.
questions.explain_vi: Khi xung đột, luật Úc được ưu tiên. Luật tôn giáo không có vị thế pháp lý.

questions.question: Should people living in Australia make an effort to learn English?

options.text: Yes. English is the national language and helps education, work and community life
Only if they want a government job

questions.explain_en: Citizenship applicants undertake to make reasonable efforts to learn English if it is not their native language.
questions.explain_vi: Người xin nhập tịch cam kết nỗ lực học tiếng Anh nếu đó không phải tiếng mẹ đẻ.

questions.question: What should you do if you suspect a friend or neighbour may be planning a serious crime?

options.text: Ignore it because it is not your business
Report it to Australian government authorities as soon as possible
Post about it on social media only

questions.explain_en: Australians have a responsibility to help keep society safe by reporting suspected serious crime.
questions.explain_vi: Nên báo cáo cho nhà chức trách càng sớm càng tốt để bảo vệ cộng đồng.

questions.question: Who are Australia’s first inhabitants?

options.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples

questions.explain_en: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples have the oldest continuous cultures in the world.
questions.explain_vi: Thổ dân bản địa và người đảo eo biển Torres là cư dân đầu tiên của Úc.

questions.question: Where are Torres Strait Islander peoples from?

options.text: Islands between the northern tip of Queensland and Papua New Guinea

questions.explain_en: Torres Strait Islander people are from islands between the tip of Queensland and PNG.
questions.explain_vi: Người đảo eo biển Torres đến từ các đảo giữa mũi Queensland và Papua New Guinea.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Victoria?
questions.explain_en: Melbourne is the capital of Victoria.
questions.explain_vi: Melbourne là thủ phủ Victoria.

questions.question: What do the seven points of the Commonwealth Star on the Australian National Flag represent?

options.text: The six states and one point for the territories

questions.explain_en: Six points are the states; the seventh is for the territories.
questions.explain_vi: Sáu cánh cho sáu tiểu bang, một cánh cho các lãnh thổ.

questions.question: On which date is Anzac Day commemorated?
questions.explain_en: Anzac Day is 25 April, the date of the 1915 Gallipoli landing.
questions.explain_vi: Ngày Anzac là 25/04, ngày đổ bộ Gallipoli năm 1915.

questions.question: In Australia, people are free to criticise the government as long as they:

options.text: Get written permission from the Prime Minister

questions.explain_en: Freedom of speech includes criticising the government, while still obeying the law.
questions.explain_vi: Tự do ngôn luận gồm việc chỉ trích chính phủ, miễn là tuân thủ luật.

questions.question: What does it mean that the Australian government is secular?

options.text: It operates separately from churches or other religious entities

questions.explain_en: Secular means government is separate from religious organisations.
questions.explain_vi: Thế tục nghĩa là chính phủ hoạt động tách biệt khỏi các tổ chức tôn giáo.

questions.question: While overseas, which privilege can Australian citizens use?

options.text: Ask for consular assistance from an Australian official while overseas
Decide which Australian laws to follow

questions.explain_en: Overseas, you can ask Australian officials for help in emergencies. You must still obey that country’s laws.
questions.explain_vi: Ở nước ngoài có thể nhờ viên chức Úc hỗ trợ lãnh sự khi cần.

questions.question: Is service in the Australian Defence Force voluntary?

options.text: No, every citizen must serve full-time
Yes, but citizens have a responsibility to defend Australia should the need arise

questions.explain_en: ADF service is voluntary. Defending Australia if needed is still a citizenship responsibility.
questions.explain_vi: Phục vụ quân đội là tự nguyện, nhưng bảo vệ Úc nếu cần vẫn là nghĩa vụ công dân.

questions.question: What is a jury?

options.text: Ordinary Australian men and women who listen to evidence and decide if a person is guilty or not guilty
The police who made the arrest

questions.explain_en: A jury is randomly chosen from the community. The judge explains the law.
questions.explain_vi: Bồi thẩm đoàn là người dân bình thường quyết định có tội hay không.

questions.question: Which body is responsible for conducting federal elections and is independent of the government?
questions.explain_en: The AEC runs federal elections and referendums and maintains the electoral roll.
questions.explain_vi: Ủy ban Bầu cử Úc (AEC) độc lập, tổ chức bầu cử liên bang.

questions.question: What is a ‘secret ballot’?

options.text: You vote privately so no one is allowed to know whom you voted for unless you tell them
The Prime Minister counts the votes in private

questions.explain_en: A secret ballot means you are free and safe to vote for any candidate.
questions.explain_vi: Bỏ phiếu kín: không ai được biết bạn bầu cho ai, trừ khi bạn nói.

questions.question: How many houses does the Australian Parliament have?

options.text: Two - the House of Representatives and the Senate

questions.explain_en: Parliament has two Houses: the House of Representatives and the Senate.
questions.explain_vi: Quốc hội Úc có lưỡng viện: Hạ viện và Thượng viện.

questions.question: What is it called when the Governor-General signs a Bill so it becomes law?
questions.explain_en: Royal Assent is the Governor-General signing a Bill into law.
questions.explain_vi: Phê chuẩn Hoàng gia (Royal Assent) là Tổng Toàn quyền ký dự luật thành luật.

questions.question: Which level of government is usually responsible for rubbish collection and local libraries?
questions.explain_en: Local councils handle local services such as rubbish, parks, local roads and libraries.
questions.explain_vi: Chính quyền địa phương lo thu rác, thư viện, đường phố địa phương.

questions.question: In Australia, can people be forced to join an organisation?

options.text: Yes, if their religion requires it
No. Individuals cannot be compelled to join or forced to leave

questions.explain_en: Freedom of association includes the right not to join.
questions.explain_vi: Không ai bị ép gia nhập hoặc bị buộc rời tổ chức.

questions.question: How should a person get a job in Australia?

options.text: Because of their wealth or ethnicity
Based on their skills and experience

questions.explain_en: The law supports selecting the person with the best skills and experience.
questions.explain_vi: Tuyển dụng dựa trên kỹ năng và kinh nghiệm, không phải giới tính, giàu có hay sắc tộc.

questions.question: Is racism accepted in Australia?

options.text: Yes, if it is posted on the internet
No. Racism has no place in Australia

questions.explain_en: Creating or sharing racially offensive material, including online or at sport, is not accepted.
questions.explain_vi: Phân biệt chủng tộc không có chỗ ở Úc, kể cả trên mạng và ở sự kiện thể thao.

questions.question: What is ‘mateship’ as described in Our Common Bond?

options.text: Helping each other in times of need
Serving only people from your own culture

questions.explain_en: Mateship is helping and receiving help, especially in difficult times. Australia has a strong volunteering tradition.
questions.explain_vi: Mateship là tinh thần giúp nhau khi khó khăn; Úc có truyền thống tình nguyện mạnh.

questions.question: Is it legal in Australia to share sexual photos or videos of someone online without their consent?

options.text: Yes, if you know the person
No. Many forms of cyber abuse are illegal
Yes, if it is a private message

questions.explain_en: Online abuse, including sharing sexual images without consent, is not accepted and many forms are illegal.
questions.explain_vi: Nhiều hình thức bạo lực trên mạng, gồm chia sẻ ảnh tình dục không đồng ý, là bất hợp pháp.

questions.question: How many states and mainland territories does Australia have?

options.text: Six states and two mainland territories

questions.explain_en: There are six states and two mainland territories (ACT and NT).
questions.explain_vi: Úc có sáu tiểu bang và hai lãnh thổ đại lục (ACT và NT).

questions.question: What is the capital city of Queensland?
questions.explain_en: Brisbane is the capital of Queensland.
questions.explain_vi: Brisbane là thủ phủ Queensland.

questions.question: What do the black and red halves of the Australian Aboriginal Flag represent?

options.text: The Aboriginal peoples (black) and the earth (red)

questions.explain_en: Black represents Aboriginal peoples; red represents the earth, which has ceremonial significance. The yellow circle is the sun.
questions.explain_vi: Đen: thổ dân bản địa. Đỏ: đất (ý nghĩa nghi lễ). Vàng: mặt trời.

questions.question: What are Australia’s national colours?
questions.explain_en: National colours are green and gold - the colours of the golden wattle.
questions.explain_vi: Màu quốc gia là xanh lá và vàng - màu hoa keo vàng.

questions.question: What is Australia’s national gemstone?
questions.explain_en: The opal is Australia’s national gemstone.
questions.explain_vi: Đá opal là đá quý quốc gia của Úc.

questions.question: Australians are expected to treat each other with dignity and respect regardless of:

options.text: Race, gender, religion, age, disability and other background
Only whether they were born in Australia

questions.explain_en: Respect applies regardless of race, origin, gender, sexual orientation, marital status, age, disability, culture, politics, wealth or religion.
questions.explain_vi: Mọi người được kỳ vọng tôn trọng nhau bất kể nguồn gốc, giới tính, tôn giáo, tuổi tác, khuyết tật, v.v.

questions.question: Which of these is both a responsibility and a privilege of Australian citizenship?

options.text: Voting in federal and state or territory elections and in a referendum
Speaking a language other than English

questions.explain_en: The book lists voting under both responsibilities and privileges.
questions.explain_vi: Đi bầu vừa là nghĩa vụ vừa là quyền lợi của công dân.

questions.question: Australian citizens aged 18 or over who are not dual citizens may:
questions.explain_en: Seeking election is a privilege, and dual citizens cannot seek election to parliament.
questions.explain_vi: Công dân 18+ không có quốc tịch kép được tranh cử vào quốc hội.

questions.question: If you travel overseas as an Australian citizen, you:

options.text: Need a visa to return to Australia
Are free to return to Australia without a visa

questions.explain_en: Citizens may apply for an Australian passport and re-enter freely.
questions.explain_vi: Công dân Úc được trở lại Úc mà không cần thị thực.

questions.question: Taxes in Australia help pay for services such as:

options.text: Government-funded healthcare and education, defence, roads and social security

questions.explain_en: Working and paying tax supports services the community enjoys.
questions.explain_vi: Thuế chi cho y tế, giáo dục, quốc phòng, đường sá và an sinh xã hội.

questions.question: Which power of government makes and changes laws?
questions.explain_en: Legislative power belongs to Parliament.
questions.explain_vi: Quyền lập pháp thuộc Quốc hội - làm và sửa luật.

questions.question: Who has judicial power in Australia?
questions.explain_en: Judges interpret and apply the law. Courts are independent of parliament and government.
questions.explain_vi: Tòa án và thẩm phán có quyền tư pháp, độc lập với quốc hội và chính phủ.

questions.question: After a federal election, the Australian Government is generally formed by:

options.text: The party or coalition with the majority of members in the House of Representatives
The party with the most senators only

questions.explain_en: The leader of that party becomes Prime Minister.
questions.explain_vi: Đảng hoặc liên minh chiếm đa số Hạ viện thành lập chính phủ; lãnh đạo trở thành Thủ tướng.

questions.question: What is a proposal for a new law or a change to a law called?
questions.explain_en: If a member of parliament proposes a new or changed law, that proposal is a Bill.
questions.explain_vi: Đề xuất luật mới hoặc sửa luật được gọi là Dự luật (Bill).

questions.question: If you do not vote in an election and do not have a good reason, you may:

options.text: Be sent to jail for 10 years

questions.explain_en: Compulsory voting is enforced with a possible fine if you have no good reason.
questions.explain_vi: Không đi bầu mà không có lý do chính đáng có thể bị phạt tiền.

questions.question: Are men and women treated equally in Australian courts of law?

options.text: Yes. Both have equal access to education, employment, voting and the courts
Only if they were born in Australia

questions.explain_en: Men and women have equal rights and equal access to education, jobs, voting, parliament, the ADF, police and the courts.
questions.explain_vi: Nam và nữ bình đẳng trước pháp luật và trong giáo dục, việc làm, bầu cử.

questions.question: Is divorce accepted in Australia?

options.text: Yes. Either a husband or a wife may apply, even if the other spouse wants to continue the marriage

questions.explain_en: Divorce is acceptable. Either spouse may apply to the courts.
questions.explain_vi: Ly hôn được chấp nhận. Chồng hoặc vợ đều có thể nộp đơn.

questions.question: Should you obey a lawful request from the police in Australia?

options.text: Yes, because all Australians commit to following the law
Only if you are not a citizen

questions.explain_en: The lawful actions of the police should be supported.
questions.explain_vi: Cần tuân theo yêu cầu hợp pháp của cảnh sát.

questions.question: What should a person do if they see or know a child is being abused?

options.text: Keep it secret to protect the family
Report it to the police to investigate

questions.explain_en: Child abuse should be reported to the police.
questions.explain_vi: Nếu biết trẻ bị lạm dụng, hãy báo cảnh sát.

questions.question: Can an Australian citizen also be a citizen of another country?

options.text: Yes, if the laws of that other country allow it - but they must still follow Australian laws in Australia
Yes, and then Australian laws no longer apply

questions.explain_en: Dual or multiple citizenship is allowed if other countries allow it. Australian law still applies in Australia.
questions.explain_vi: Được giữ quốc tịch kép nếu nước kia cho phép; ở Úc vẫn phải tuân luật Úc.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Western Australia?
questions.explain_en: Perth is the capital of Western Australia, the largest state.
questions.explain_vi: Perth là thủ phủ Tây Úc.

questions.question: What is the capital city of the Northern Territory?
questions.explain_en: Darwin is the capital of the Northern Territory.
questions.explain_vi: Darwin là thủ phủ Lãnh thổ Bắc Úc.

questions.question: Which animals support the shield on the Commonwealth Coat of Arms?
questions.explain_en: A kangaroo and an emu, both native Australian animals, support the shield.
questions.explain_vi: Chuột túi và đà điểu emu đỡ tấm khiên Quốc huy.

questions.question: Who usually performs a Welcome to Country?

options.text: An Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander custodian of the local region

questions.explain_en: A Welcome to Country is performed by a Traditional Custodian of that land.
questions.explain_vi: Chào mừng đến quê hương do người gìn giữ truyền thống của vùng đất đó thực hiện.

questions.question: During Australia Day celebrations, the Prime Minister announces:

options.text: The Australian of the Year Awards in Canberra
The date of the next election

questions.explain_en: The Australian of the Year Awards are announced in Canberra on Australia Day.
questions.explain_vi: Thủ tướng công bố Danh hiệu Người Úc trong Năm tại Canberra vào ngày Quốc khánh.

questions.question: Freedom of expression includes expressing views through:
questions.explain_en: People can express views through art, film, music and literature, while obeying the law.
questions.explain_vi: Tự do biểu đạt gồm nghệ thuật, phim, nhạc, văn - vẫn phải tuân luật.

questions.question: Australia has public holidays on Christian days such as:

options.text: Good Friday, Easter Sunday and Christmas Day

questions.explain_en: Australia has a Judaeo-Christian heritage and holidays on those Christian days, but no official national religion.
questions.explain_vi: Úc có ngày lễ Thứ Sáu Tốt lành, Chủ Nhật Phục sinh và Giáng sinh; vẫn không có quốc giáo.

questions.question: Australian citizens can apply for a job in:

options.text: The Australian Public Service and the Australian Defence Force

questions.explain_en: A privilege of citizenship is applying for APS jobs (e.g. Services Australia, ATO) and the ADF.
questions.explain_vi: Công dân được xin việc trong bộ máy công quyền và lực lượng quốc phòng.

questions.question: When you are in another country, you must:

options.text: Obey the laws of that country

questions.explain_en: While overseas you must obey that country’s laws. Some Australian laws also apply to Australians overseas.
questions.explain_vi: Khi ở nước khác phải chấp hành luật nước đó.

questions.question: Is voting compulsory in local government elections in every state?

options.text: It may not be compulsory in some states

questions.explain_en: Voting is compulsory federally and in state/territory elections. Local voting may not be compulsory in some states.
questions.explain_vi: Bầu cử địa phương ở một số tiểu bang có thể không bắt buộc.

questions.question: Australia is a constitutional monarchy. This means:

options.text: The King is Head of State but must act in accordance with the Constitution
The King makes laws every day in Canberra

questions.explain_en: The King’s powers in Australia are delegated to the Governor-General. The King does not have a day-to-day role.
questions.explain_vi: Quốc vương là nguyên thủ nhưng phải theo Hiến pháp; quyền được giao cho Tổng Toàn quyền.

questions.question: Which of these is a role of the Governor-General?

options.text: Leading a political party in elections
Signing Bills passed by Parliament into law
Deciding criminal guilt instead of a court

questions.explain_en: The Governor-General signs Bills (Royal Assent), stays neutral, and is not part of the government.
questions.explain_vi: Tổng Toàn quyền ký dự luật thành luật và phải trung lập.

questions.question: How many senators are there in the Australian Senate?
questions.explain_en: There are 76 senators: 12 per state and 2 each for the ACT and NT.
questions.explain_vi: Thượng viện có 76 nghị sĩ: 12 mỗi tiểu bang, 2 cho ACT và 2 cho NT.

questions.question: What is the leader of a territory government called?
questions.explain_en: Territory governments are led by a Chief Minister.
questions.explain_vi: Lãnh đạo chính phủ lãnh thổ là Thủ hiến lãnh thổ (Chief Minister).

questions.question: In Australia’s court system, people are considered:

options.text: Guilty until they prove they are innocent
Innocent until they are found guilty in a court
Guilty if the police arrest them

questions.explain_en: Everyone has the right to be represented by a lawyer. The court decides guilt.
questions.explain_vi: Mọi người được coi là vô tội cho đến khi bị kết tội tại tòa.

questions.question: Is it acceptable to promote violence against people because of their culture, ethnicity or religion?

options.text: Never. It is against Australian values and law

questions.explain_en: Promoting violence against a person or group is never acceptable.
questions.explain_vi: Thúc đẩy bạo lực vì văn hóa, sắc tộc hay tôn giáo là trái giá trị và luật Úc.

questions.question: Is physical violence against a spouse or partner ever acceptable in Australia?

options.text: Yes, if it stays inside the home
Never. It is a criminal offence
Yes, if the couple is married

questions.explain_en: Violence against a spouse or partner is never acceptable and is a crime.
questions.explain_vi: Bạo lực với vợ/chồng hay bạn đời không bao giờ được chấp nhận và là tội phạm.

questions.question: Australians value listening to others and respecting their views even when they disagree. This is called:
questions.explain_en: People should be tolerant where they disagree and have the right to be safe from violence.
questions.explain_vi: Tôn trọng lẫn nhau và khoan dung: lắng nghe và tôn trọng ý kiến khác.

questions.question: Australians expect everyone living in Australia to:

options.text: Participate in society and make a contribution when they can
Avoid work if they can live on other people’s money only
Stay only within their own cultural group

questions.explain_en: Everyone has a responsibility to try to support themselves and their families when they are able.
questions.explain_vi: Mọi người được mong đợi tham gia cộng đồng và tự hỗ trợ bản thân khi có thể.

questions.question: Using social media to share official government secrets would:

options.text: Be a normal part of freedom of speech
Be required of all new citizens

questions.explain_en: Australian society is based on shared obligations not to undermine Australia’s interests and security.
questions.explain_vi: Chia sẻ bí mật chính phủ trên mạng là làm suy yếu lợi ích Úc.

questions.question: According to archaeology, Aboriginal peoples arrived in Australia:
questions.explain_en: The archaeological record indicates arrival between 65,000 and 40,000 years ago.
questions.explain_vi: Khảo cổ cho thấy thổ dân bản địa đến Úc khoảng 65.000-40.000 năm trước.

questions.question: After the gold rush began in 1851, Australia’s population:
questions.explain_en: In 10 years, Australia’s population more than doubled.
questions.explain_vi: Trong 10 năm, dân số Úc tăng hơn gấp đôi.

questions.question: How many distinct Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages are also valued in Australia?
questions.explain_en: Other languages are valued, including more than 100 distinct Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages.
questions.explain_vi: Hơn 100 ngôn ngữ thổ dân bản địa và dân đảo Torres Strait riêng biệt cũng được coi trọng.

questions.question: Which state is separated from mainland Australia by Bass Strait?
questions.explain_en: Tasmania is separated from the mainland by Bass Strait.
questions.explain_vi: Tasmania ngăn cách đất liền bởi eo biển Bass.

questions.question: On Australia Day, the Prime Minister announces the Australian of the Year Awards in:
questions.explain_en: The awards are announced in Canberra on Australia Day.
questions.explain_vi: Giải Australian of the Year được công bố tại Canberra vào Australia Day.

questions.question: Anzac Day is named after the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps landing at Gallipoli in:
questions.explain_en: Anzac Day commemorates the 25 April 1915 Gallipoli landing in Türkiye.
questions.explain_vi: Anzac tưởng nhớ đổ bộ Gallipoli ngày 25/04/1915 tại Türkiye.

questions.question: What is Australia’s national gemstone?
questions.explain_en: The opal is Australia’s national gemstone.
questions.explain_vi: Opal là đá quý quốc gia của Úc.

questions.question: Australia has public holidays on Christian days such as:

options.text: Good Friday, Easter Sunday and Christmas Day

questions.explain_en: Australia has a Judaeo-Christian heritage and those Christian holidays, but no official national religion.
questions.explain_vi: Úc có ngày nghỉ Good Friday, Easter Sunday và Christmas Day, nhưng không có quốc giáo.

questions.question: Freedom of expression in Australia includes expressing views through:
questions.explain_en: Freedom of expression covers art, film, music and literature, while obeying the law.
questions.explain_vi: Tự do biểu đạt gồm nghệ thuật, phim, nhạc và văn học, miễn tuân thủ luật.

questions.question: Paying tax in Australia is:

options.text: Required by law and helps fund community services

questions.explain_en: Tax is required by law and supports services such as healthcare and education.
questions.explain_vi: Nộp thuế là bắt buộc theo luật và tài trợ dịch vụ cộng đồng.

questions.question: Who is the leader of a local government area?
questions.explain_en: A Mayor or Shire President leads a local government.
questions.explain_vi: Mayor hoặc Shire President lãnh đạo chính quyền địa phương.

questions.question: In a car in Australia, which traffic rule is stated in Our Common Bond?

options.text: Everybody must wear a seatbelt; babies and young children need an approved car seat
Only the driver needs a seatbelt

questions.explain_en: Everybody travelling in a car must wear a seatbelt; babies and young children must be in an approved car seat.
questions.explain_vi: Mọi người trong xe phải thắt dây an toàn; trẻ nhỏ cần ghế chuyên dụng.

questions.question: Australian citizens can raise concerns about government policy by:
questions.explain_en: Citizens can contact their elected representative about laws and policy.
questions.explain_vi: Công dân có thể liên hệ đại diện được bầu về luật và chính sách.

questions.question: Which power of government makes and changes laws?
questions.explain_en: Legislative power is the power to make laws, held by Parliament.
questions.explain_vi: Quyền lập pháp thuộc Quốc hội: làm và sửa luật.

questions.question: After a federal election, the Opposition is generally:

options.text: The party or coalition with the second largest number of members in the House of Representatives

questions.explain_en: The second largest group in the House of Representatives forms the Opposition.
questions.explain_vi: Nhóm lớn thứ hai ở Hạ viện thành Đối lập.

questions.question: Is cyber abuse, such as sharing sexual photos online without consent, accepted in Australia?

options.text: No. Many forms of cyber abuse are illegal
Yes, if the person is overseas

questions.explain_en: Online abuse is not accepted; many forms of cyber abuse are illegal.
questions.explain_vi: Bạo lực trên mạng không được chấp nhận; nhiều hình thức là bất hợp pháp.

questions.question: Should people in Australia obey a lawful request from the police?

options.text: Yes, because Australians commit to following the law
Only if they agree with the request

questions.explain_en: The lawful actions of the police should be supported; obey lawful requests.
questions.explain_vi: Phải tuân theo yêu cầu hợp pháp của cảnh sát.

questions.question: What does a ‘fair go’ mean in Australia?

options.text: Success should come from talent, work and effort, not wealth or background
Jobs must go to family members

questions.explain_en: A fair go means equal opportunity based on talent, work and effort.
questions.explain_vi: Fair go nghĩa là cơ hội công bằng nhờ tài năng, làm việc và nỗ lực.

questions.question: Is polygamy (being married to more than one person at the same time) legal in Australia?
questions.explain_en: Polygamy is against the law in Australia and can result in severe penalties.
questions.explain_vi: Đa thê là tội ở Úc.

questions.question: Religious laws in Australia:

options.text: Have no legal status; Australian law must be followed

questions.explain_en: Religious laws have no legal status in Australia.
questions.explain_vi: Luật tôn giáo không có giá trị pháp lý ở Úc.

questions.question: Aboriginal peoples believe their creation stories commence with:
questions.explain_en: Aboriginal peoples believe their creation stories commence with the beginning of time.
questions.explain_vi: Thổ dân bản địa tin creation stories bắt đầu từ khởi thuỷ của thời gian.

questions.question: Before Federation, Australia was made up of:
questions.explain_en: Before 1901 Australia was six separate, self-governing British colonies.
questions.explain_vi: Trước 1901 Úc gồm sáu thuộc địa Anh riêng.

questions.question: Which is Australia’s largest state?
questions.explain_en: Western Australia is the largest state.
questions.explain_vi: Western Australia là tiểu bang lớn nhất.

questions.question: Which is Australia’s smallest mainland state?
questions.explain_en: Victoria is the smallest of the mainland states.
questions.explain_vi: Victoria là tiểu bang đất liền nhỏ nhất.

questions.question: Canberra is located:
questions.explain_en: The ACT sits between Sydney and Melbourne and is home to the national capital.
questions.explain_vi: ACT nằm giữa Sydney và Melbourne; Canberra là thủ đô quốc gia.

questions.question: What do the kangaroo and emu on the Commonwealth Coat of Arms represent?

options.text: Native Australian animals supporting the shield

questions.explain_en: A kangaroo and an emu support the shield; both are native Australian animals.
questions.explain_vi: Kangaroo và emu chống hai bên khiên; đều là động vật bản địa Úc.

questions.question: Australia’s national colours are:
questions.explain_en: National colours are green and gold - the colours of the golden wattle.
questions.explain_vi: Màu quốc gia là xanh lá và vàng.

questions.question: Volunteering in Australia is described as:

options.text: A way to avoid paying tax
Part of mateship and community service

questions.explain_en: Australia has a strong tradition of community service and volunteering in the spirit of mateship.
questions.explain_vi: Tình nguyện thuộc tinh thần mateship và phục vụ cộng đồng.

questions.question: Does Australia have an official national religion?
questions.explain_en: Australia has no official national religion; the government is secular.
questions.explain_vi: Úc không có quốc giáo; chính phủ thế tục.

questions.question: Cabinet is:

options.text: Ministers with the most important portfolios; the key decision-making body of government

questions.explain_en: Ministers with the most important portfolios make up the Cabinet.
questions.explain_vi: Cabinet gồm các bộ trưởng quan trọng nhất; cơ quan quyết định chính.

questions.question: A proposal for a new law in the Australian Parliament is called a:
questions.explain_en: A proposal to introduce or change a law is called a Bill.
questions.explain_vi: Đề xuất luật mới gọi là Bill (dự luật).

questions.question: An elected member of a local council is called a:
questions.explain_en: Citizens elect local councillors.
questions.explain_vi: Thành viên hội đồng địa phương được bầu gọi là Councillor.

questions.question: In the Northern Territory, an Administrator is appointed by:
questions.explain_en: In the NT, an Administrator is appointed by the Governor-General.
questions.explain_vi: Administrator ở NT do Toàn quyền bổ nhiệm.

questions.question: Every person in an Australian court has the right to be represented by a:
questions.explain_en: Every person has the right to be represented by a lawyer in court.
questions.explain_vi: Mọi người có quyền được luật sư đại diện tại tòa.

questions.question: Road and traffic rules are controlled by:
questions.explain_en: Road and traffic rules are controlled by state and territory governments.
questions.explain_vi: Luật giao thông do chính quyền tiểu bang và lãnh thổ quản lý.

questions.question: Is racism accepted in Australia?

options.text: No. Racism has no place in Australia

questions.explain_en: Racism has no place in Australia and is against the law.
questions.explain_vi: Phân biệt chủng tộc không có chỗ ở Úc.

questions.question: People living in Australia should make an effort to learn:
questions.explain_en: English is the national language and an important unifying element.
questions.explain_vi: Nên nỗ lực học tiếng Anh, ngôn ngữ quốc gia.

questions.question: If you suspect a neighbour may be planning a serious crime, you should:

options.text: Report it to Australian government authorities as soon as possible

questions.explain_en: Report suspected serious crime to authorities to help keep the community safe.
questions.explain_vi: Báo nhà chức trách càng sớm càng tốt.

questions.question: Men and women in Australia:

options.text: Have equal rights, including equal access to education and employment

questions.explain_en: Men and women have equal rights under Australian law.
questions.explain_vi: Nam nữ có quyền bình đẳng.

questions.question: Is domestic and family violence against the law in Australia?

options.text: No, if it stays in the home
Yes, it is a serious crime

questions.explain_en: Domestic and family violence is not accepted and is against the law.
questions.explain_vi: Bạo lực gia đình là tội nghiêm trọng.

questions.question: In 1901, Australia’s population was about four million. This number:

options.text: Included all Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples
Did not include Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples

questions.explain_en: Indigenous peoples were not included in official estimates until after the 1967 Referendum.
questions.explain_vi: Số 4 triệu năm 1901 không gồm thổ dân bản địa; sau trưng cầu 1967 mới được tính.

questions.question: The first large group of migrants not from Europe arrived during:

options.text: The gold rush from 1851 - Chinese people

questions.explain_en: Chinese people arriving during the gold rush were the first large non-European migrant group.
questions.explain_vi: Người Hoa thời kỳ cơn sốt Vàng 1851 là nhóm di dân lớn đầu tiên không phải người châu Âu.

questions.question: Who can deliver an Acknowledgement of Country?

options.text: Only an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander custodian of that land
Anyone - at meetings it is often the Chair or Master of Ceremonies

questions.explain_en: A Welcome to Country is by a Traditional Custodian. An Acknowledgement can be given by anyone.
questions.explain_vi: Lời cảm ơn Đất nước ai cũng có thể nói. Welcome to Country thì do người gìn giữ truyền thống.

questions.question: Which statement about the Australian National Flag is correct?

options.text: The Union Jack represents Australia’s Indigenous heritage
The Union Jack represents British settlement and the laws and institutions inherited as a result
The Southern Cross has seven points for the states

questions.explain_en: The Union Jack is the UK flag in the top left. National colours (green and gold) are not the flag colours.
questions.explain_vi: Union Jack tượng trưng những người Anh đầu tiên và luật/thể chế thừa hưởng. Màu quốc gia xanh-vàng khác màu cờ.

questions.question: Which state is separated from the mainland by Bass Strait?
questions.explain_en: Tasmania is the smallest state, separated by Bass Strait. Its capital is Hobart.
questions.explain_vi: Tasmania tách khỏi đất liền bởi eo biển Bass; thủ phủ Hobart.

questions.question: A person who is a dual citizen wants to seek election to an Australian parliament. What does the book say?

options.text: They can seek election at any level
They must be 18 or over and must not be dual citizens
Only the King can approve it

questions.explain_en: Seeking election: aged 18 or over and not dual citizens. Dual citizenship itself is otherwise allowed.
questions.explain_vi: Tranh cử: đủ 18 tuổi và không có quốc tịch kép. Giữ quốc tịch kép vẫn được, nhưng không được ứng cử.

questions.question: Which statement about voting is correct?

options.text: Voting is compulsory in federal and state or territory elections; local elections may not be compulsory in some states
Voting is optional at every level
Voting is compulsory in local elections in every state but optional federally

questions.explain_en: This is a common trap: local government voting is not always compulsory.
questions.explain_vi: Bẫy thường gặp: bầu cử hội đồng địa phương không phải lúc nào cũng bắt buộc.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a responsibility of Australian citizens?

options.text: Vote in federal and state or territory elections and in a referendum

questions.explain_en: Joining a party is a freedom, not a duty. The four responsibilities are obey, vote, defend, jury.
questions.explain_vi: Vào đảng là quyền tự do, không phải nghĩa vụ bắt buộc.

questions.question: Peaceful gatherings to protest must:

options.text: Be allowed to injure people if the cause is important
Stay peaceful and not injure any person or damage property

questions.explain_en: Freedom of association and protest always require obedience to Australian law.
questions.explain_vi: Tụ tập phản đối phải ôn hòa, không gây thương tích hay phá tài sản.

questions.question: To change the Australian Constitution, a referendum needs a ‘double majority’. This means:

options.text: A majority of ministers and a majority of judges
A majority of voters in a majority of states AND a majority of voters across the nation
A majority in the Senate twice

questions.explain_en: Both the national majority and a majority of voters in a majority of states must vote for the change.
questions.explain_vi: Đa số kép: đa số cử tri toàn quốc VÀ đa số cử tri ở đa số tiểu bang.

questions.question: Which statement about states and territories is correct?

options.text: Territories have the same constitutional rights as states
States have rights recognised by the Constitution; territory laws can be altered or revoked by the Australian Government at any time
Territories elect 12 senators each, the same as states

questions.explain_en: States have constitutional rights; territories do not. ACT and NT elect two senators each, not 12.
questions.explain_vi: Tiểu bang có quyền trong Hiến pháp; luật lãnh thổ có thể bị chính phủ liên bang sửa hoặc hủy.

questions.question: Who decides if a person is guilty in court, and who decides the penalty in a criminal trial after a guilty verdict?

options.text: The jury decides guilt; the judge decides the penalty
The judge decides guilt; the jury decides the penalty

questions.explain_en: The jury decides innocent or guilty. If guilty, the judge decides the penalty.
questions.explain_vi: Bồi thẩm đoàn quyết định có tội hay không; thẩm phán quyết định hình phạt.

questions.question: The Australian Federal Police (AFP) is responsible for:

options.text: All local parking fines in every suburb
Crimes against federal laws (for example drug trafficking and national security) and general police work in the ACT

questions.explain_en: State and NT police handle state/territory crimes. AFP also does general policing in the ACT.
questions.explain_vi: AFP điều tra tội liên bang và cũng làm cảnh sát thường tại ACT.

questions.question: Which of the following is a federal responsibility, not a typical local-council responsibility?
questions.explain_en: Defence is an Australian Government responsibility. Pools, signs and rubbish are local.
questions.explain_vi: Quốc phòng thuộc liên bang. Hồ bơi, biển báo, rác thuộc địa phương.

questions.question: The Governor-General must:

options.text: Remain neutral and is not part of the government
Sit in the House of Representatives

questions.explain_en: The Governor-General is the King’s representative, acts independently of all political parties, and stays neutral.
questions.explain_vi: Tổng Toàn quyền không thuộc chính phủ và phải trung lập.

questions.question: A person says a religious law allows them to have more than one spouse at the same time. In Australia:

options.text: Religious law is accepted if both families agree
Polygamy is against the law and can result in severe penalties, including imprisonment
Polygamy is legal for some religions only

questions.explain_en: Religious laws have no legal status. Polygamy and forced marriage are crimes.
questions.explain_vi: Đa thê và ép cưới là tội ở Úc, dù tôn giáo cho phép.

questions.question: Can two people of the same sex marry each other under Australian law?

options.text: Yes. Two people can marry each other, including two men or two women

questions.explain_en: The book states that under our laws two people can marry, including two men or two women.
questions.explain_vi: Luật Úc cho phép hai người kết hôn, gồm hai nam hoặc hai nữ.

questions.question: A 20-year-old man wants a sexual relationship with a 15-year-old girl. In Australia this is:

options.text: Against the law in all Australian states and territories

questions.explain_en: Age of consent is 16 or 17 depending on the state or territory. 15 is below the age of consent everywhere.
questions.explain_vi: Độ tuổi đồng ý là 16 hoặc 17 tùy bang. Quan hệ với người 15 tuổi là trái luật mọi nơi.

questions.question: If a woman has better qualifications and skills than a man for a job:

options.text: The man should still get the job
It is a right for the woman to get the job

questions.explain_en: It is against the law to discriminate because of gender. The better-qualified woman should get the job.
questions.explain_vi: Phụ nữ có quyền nhận việc nếu có trình độ và kỹ năng tốt hơn.

questions.question: An Australian citizen is overseas. Which statement is true?

options.text: No Australian criminal laws apply outside Australia
Some Australian laws must still be followed overseas - for example it is illegal to be involved in sexual activity with a child under 16, here or overseas

questions.explain_en: Some Australian laws follow citizens overseas, including child sex offences under 16.
questions.explain_vi: Một số luật Úc vẫn áp dụng khi công dân ở nước ngoài, gồm quan hệ tình dục với trẻ dưới 16 tuổi.

questions.question: The archaeological record indicates Aboriginal peoples arrived in Australia:
questions.explain_en: Aboriginal peoples believe their creation stories commence with the beginning of time.
questions.explain_vi: Thổ dân bản địa đến Úc khoảng 65.000-40.000 năm trước.

questions.question: Which combination of dates is correct?

options.text: First Fleet 26 January 1788; Federation 1 January 1901; Gallipoli landing 25 April 1915
First Fleet 25 April 1915; Federation 26 January 1788; gold rush 1967

questions.explain_en: Keep 1788, 1901 and 25 April 1915 separate. Australia Day commemorates 26 January 1788, not Federation.

questions.question: Which is the smallest of the mainland states?
questions.explain_en: Victoria is the smallest mainland state. Tasmania is smaller overall but is an island, not mainland.
questions.explain_vi: Victoria là tiểu bang đất liền nhỏ nhất. Tasmania nhỏ hơn nhưng là đảo.

questions.question: On the Torres Strait Islander Flag, what does the white dancer’s headdress symbolise?

options.text: A symbol for all Torres Strait Islanders

questions.explain_en: Green is land, blue is sea, black lines are the people, white headdress is for all Torres Strait Islanders, white star is island groups and peace.
questions.explain_vi: Mũ vũ công trắng là biểu tượng cho tất cả người đảo eo biển Torres.

questions.question: After World War II, a large wave of migration to Australia came mainly from:

options.text: Europe - millions of people had to leave their homelands

questions.explain_en: A wave of non-British European migration came after WWII.
questions.explain_vi: Sau Thế chiến II có làn sóng di dân châu Âu không phải người Anh.

questions.question: The Rule of Law says no person, group or ________ is above the law.
questions.explain_en: No person, group or religious rule is above the law.
questions.explain_vi: Không có người, nhóm hay quy định tôn giáo nào đứng trên pháp luật.

questions.question: Which statement about jury service is correct?

options.text: Only lawyers may sit on a jury
Citizens on the electoral roll can be called; the jury decides guilty or not guilty
The jury also always decides the prison sentence

questions.explain_en: Jury service helps keep the court system open and fair. The judge decides the penalty after a guilty verdict.
questions.explain_vi: Công dân trong danh sách bầu cử có thể được gọi bồi thẩm. Họ quyết định có tội hay không.

questions.question: Which privilege is listed for Australian citizens?

options.text: Apply for work in the Australian Public Service, for example Services Australia or the ATO
Choose not to enrol if they dislike politics
Use religious law instead of Australian law in court

questions.explain_en: APS and ADF jobs are privileges of citizenship.
questions.explain_vi: Xin việc trong Dịch vụ công cộng Úc (ví dụ Services Australia, ATO) là quyền lợi.

questions.question: Before 1901, the six colonies each had their own laws on defence, immigration, postage, trade and transport. This caused problems because:

options.text: There was already one national parliament
Trade and transport between colonies was expensive and slow, and defence was weak

questions.explain_en: Those difficulties were a reason people wanted one nation. Federation was 1 January 1901.
questions.explain_vi: Thương mại và giao thông giữa thuộc địa chậm và đắt; quốc phòng yếu - nên hợp nhất năm 1901.

questions.question: The Australian Constitution originally passed as part of:

options.text: A British Act of Parliament in 1900, and came into effect on 1 January 1901
A local council vote in Sydney in 1788

questions.explain_en: The Constitution Act 1900 was a British Act; it took effect when the colonies became one nation on 1 January 1901.
questions.explain_vi: Hiến pháp được thông qua như Đạo luật Anh năm 1900, có hiệu lực 01/01/1901.

questions.question: How are seats in the House of Representatives allocated?

options.text: Every state gets the same number of MPs
The number of MPs for each state and territory is based on the number of people there

questions.explain_en: There are over 150 members. This is the opposite of the Senate, where states are equal.
questions.explain_vi: Số ghế Hạ viện theo dân số. Thượng viện thì các tiểu bang ngang nhau.

questions.question: Who approves the appointment of the Prime Minister and ministers?
questions.explain_en: The PM recommends ministers. The Governor-General approves the PM and ministers.
questions.explain_vi: Thủ tướng đề xuất bộ trưởng; Tổng Toàn quyền phê chuẩn.

questions.question: Offering a bribe to a police officer in Australia is:

options.text: A serious crime - even offering a bribe is a crime
Legal if the amount is small

questions.explain_en: It is a serious crime to bribe the police or even to offer a bribe.
questions.explain_vi: Hối lộ cảnh sát - kể cả chỉ đề nghị - là tội nghiêm trọng.

questions.question: Can the government take a judge’s job away because it disagrees with a decision?

options.text: No. Judges are independent. The government cannot take their jobs away if it disagrees
Yes, but only in the territories

questions.explain_en: Judges and magistrates are appointed by government but cannot be removed for disagreeing.
questions.explain_vi: Chính phủ không thể cách chức thẩm phán vì không đồng ý với phán quyết.

questions.question: In the Northern Territory, an Administrator is appointed by:
questions.explain_en: The Administrator’s role is similar to a state Governor.
questions.explain_vi: Chánh Văn phòng NT do Tổng Toàn quyền bổ nhiệm, vai trò giống Toàn quyền tiểu bang.

questions.question: Forced marriage in Australia is:

options.text: Against the law and can result in severe legal penalties, including imprisonment
A religious matter only, not a crime

questions.explain_en: A forced marriage is one where one or both people did not have a free choice.
questions.explain_vi: Ép cưới là tội, có thể bị phạt nặng kể cả tù.

questions.question: People of different faiths in Australia, for example Buddhists and Christians:

options.text: Must receive the same treatment under the law
May be given preferential treatment if they are a majority

questions.explain_en: People from different backgrounds are not given preferential treatment, nor discriminated against.
questions.explain_vi: Phật tử và các tín ngưỡng khác được đối xử như người theo Thiên chúa giáo.

questions.question: Making false allegations, or encouraging others to break the law, is:

options.text: A normal part of freedom of speech

questions.explain_en: Freedom of speech does not include false allegations or encouraging others to break the law.
questions.explain_vi: Vu cáo hoặc xúi người khác phạm pháp là bất hợp pháp.

questions.question: Both men and women have the right to make independent choices about:

options.text: Marriage and religion, and are protected from intimidation or violence
Whether children must go to school

questions.explain_en: Personal matters such as marriage and religion are independent choices protected by law.
questions.explain_vi: Nam và nữ được tự quyết việc hôn nhân và tôn giáo, được luật bảo vệ khỏi đe dọa.

questions.question: Promoting distrust in and fear of an ethnic community:

options.text: Is required in the citizenship pledge

questions.explain_en: Australian society is based on obligations not to undermine community relations or Australia’s interests.
questions.explain_vi: Gây mất lòng tin và sợ hãi với một cộng đồng sắc tộc làm tổn hại quan hệ cộng đồng Úc.

questions.question: In 10 years after the 1851 gold rush, Australia’s population:
questions.explain_en: People came from around the world; population more than doubled in 10 years.
questions.explain_vi: Trong 10 năm sau Thời kỳ cơn sốt Vàng, dân số Úc tăng hơn gấp đôi.

questions.question: Early free settlers came mainly from:
questions.explain_en: British and Irish heritage has had a major influence on Australia’s recent history, culture and politics.
questions.explain_vi: Di dân tự do đầu tiên chủ yếu từ Anh và Ireland.

questions.question: Which icons are associated with the Northern Territory in the book?

options.text: Sydney Harbour Bridge and the Opera House
Uluru, Kata Tjuta and Kings Canyon

questions.explain_en: NT: tropical north, red desert south, capital Darwin; icons Uluru, Kata Tjuta, Kings Canyon.
questions.explain_vi: Biểu tượng NT gồm Uluru, Kata Tjuta và Kings Canyon.

questions.question: The Commonwealth Star sits:

options.text: On the right of the flag, as part of the Southern Cross
Under the Union Jack, with seven points
In the centre of the Aboriginal Flag

questions.explain_en: Do not confuse the Commonwealth Star (7 points, under the Union Jack) with the Southern Cross.
questions.explain_vi: Ngôi sao Liên bang 7 cánh nằm dưới Union Jack, không phải chòm Nam Thập Tự.

questions.question: A Welcome to Country is usually:

options.text: The last item at an event
The first item of proceedings to open an event

questions.explain_en: It can include songs, dances, smoking ceremonies or speeches.
questions.explain_vi: Welcome to Country thường là tiết mục đầu tiên khai mạc sự kiện.

questions.question: Which statement about defending Australia is most accurate?

options.text: Every citizen must join the ADF full-time
ADF service is voluntary, but citizens have a responsibility to defend Australia should the need arise

questions.explain_en: Voluntary service vs the responsibility to defend if needed is a common mix-up.
questions.explain_vi: Quân đội tự nguyện, nhưng bảo vệ đất nước khi cần vẫn là nghĩa vụ công dân.

questions.question: Australian officials overseas can help citizens with:

options.text: An emergency passport and support in accident, serious illness or death
Permission to ignore that country’s laws
A seat in that country’s parliament

questions.explain_en: Help also covers emergencies such as civil unrest and natural disasters. You must still obey local laws.
questions.explain_vi: Viên chức Úc có thể cấp hộ chiếu khẩn và hỗ trợ tai nạn, bệnh nặng, qua đời.

questions.question: Paying tax is:

options.text: Required by law on money you earn from a job, business or investments
Only for people who own a house

questions.explain_en: There are also taxes on many goods and services. State, territory and local governments also collect taxes.
questions.explain_vi: Nộp thuế là bắt buộc theo luật, từ lương, kinh doanh hoặc đầu tư.

questions.question: Which names are also used for the Senate?

options.text: Upper House, House of Review, or States’ House

questions.explain_en: The House of Representatives is the Lower House / People’s House. Do not swap the nicknames.
questions.explain_vi: Thượng viện còn gọi Thượng nghị viện, Viện xem xét, Viện các bang.

questions.question: The Opposition after a federal election is:

options.text: The party or coalition with the second largest number of members in the House of Representatives

questions.explain_en: Its leader is the Leader of the Opposition.
questions.explain_vi: Phe đối lập là đảng/liên minh có số ghế Hạ viện lớn thứ hai.

questions.question: Cabinet is:

options.text: Ministers with the most important portfolios - the key decision-making body of government

questions.explain_en: Government ministers each have a portfolio (an area of government).
questions.explain_vi: Nội các gồm các bộ trưởng then chốt - cơ quan quyết định chính của chính phủ.

questions.question: A Bill becomes law only after:

options.text: A majority in each House of Parliament agrees and the Governor-General gives Royal Assent

questions.explain_en: State and territory parliaments make their own laws in a similar way.
questions.explain_vi: Đa số mỗi viện đồng ý, rồi Tổng Toàn quyền phê chuẩn Hoàng gia.

questions.question: The police may arrest someone and give evidence in court. Who decides if that person is guilty?

options.text: The police officer who made the arrest

questions.explain_en: Police maintain peace and are independent of government, but they do not decide guilt.
questions.explain_vi: Cảnh sát có thể bắt và đưa ra bằng chứng; tòa quyết định có tội hay không.

questions.question: Not knowing an Australian law is:

options.text: No excuse - you could still be charged
Only an excuse in the first year of citizenship

questions.explain_en: If you break a law you did not know about, you could still be charged.
questions.explain_vi: Không biết luật không phải lý do bào chữa.

questions.question: Which traffic rule is stated in the book?

options.text: Everybody in a car must wear a seatbelt; babies and young children must be in an approved car seat
You may use a hand-held mobile while driving if the road is empty

questions.explain_en: You need a local driver’s licence and a registered car. Drug/alcohol limits and hand-held mobiles are also covered.
questions.explain_vi: Mọi người trên xe phải cài dây an toàn; trẻ nhỏ phải ghế được chấp thuận.

questions.question: Religious intolerance in Australian society is:

options.text: Accepted if you are in the majority religion
Not acceptable. People should have equal opportunity regardless of ethnicity or religion, while obeying Australian law

questions.explain_en: The government treats all citizens equally, whatever their religion or beliefs.
questions.explain_vi: Không khoan dung tôn giáo là không được chấp nhận.

questions.question: Newspapers, television and radio in Australia:

options.text: Have the same freedom of speech, so long as they stay within the law

questions.explain_en: Media have the same freedom to say and write about topics and discuss ideas.
questions.explain_vi: Báo, đài truyền hình và phát thanh cũng có tự do ngôn luận trong khuôn khổ luật.

questions.question: The age of consent in Australia is:

options.text: 16 or 17, depending on which state or territory you reside in
18 everywhere, with no exceptions stated in the book

questions.explain_en: There is no single national number. 15 is below the age of consent in all states and territories.
questions.explain_vi: Tuổi đồng ý là 16 hoặc 17 tùy tiểu bang/lãnh thổ - không phải một số duy nhất.

questions.question: If people disagree, Australians believe in:

options.text: Using violence to win the argument
Peaceful disagreement and the right to be safe from violence and intimidation
Letting religious courts settle every dispute

questions.explain_en: Verbal and physical abuse are illegal.
questions.explain_vi: Người Úc tin bất đồng ôn hòa và quyền được an toàn, không bị bạo lực.

questions.question: Citizenship applicants whose native language is not English must undertake to:

options.text: Make reasonable efforts to learn the English language

questions.explain_en: English is a unifying element of society and is essential for economic participation and social cohesion.
questions.explain_vi: Người xin nhập tịch cam kết nỗ lực hợp lý để học tiếng Anh.

questions.question: Historically, Aboriginal people are from:
questions.explain_en: Torres Strait Islander people are from the islands between Queensland and PNG.
questions.explain_vi: Thổ dân bản địa đến từ đất liền Úc và Tasmania.

questions.question: Other languages in Australia are valued, including:

options.text: More than 100 distinct Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages

questions.explain_en: English is the national language; other languages are also valued.
questions.explain_vi: Hơn 100 ngôn ngữ thổ dân bản địa và người đảo eo biển Torres riêng biệt cũng được coi trọng.

questions.question: The ACT is located:

options.text: Between Sydney and Melbourne, and is home to Parliament House and the High Court
In the far north next to Darwin

questions.explain_en: Canberra is the national capital, between Sydney and Melbourne.
questions.explain_vi: ACT nằm giữa Sydney và Melbourne; có Quốc hội và Tòa án Tối cao.

questions.question: Anzac Day remembers:

options.text: The sacrifice of all Australians who served and died in wars, conflicts and peacekeeping, and honours all servicemen and women

questions.explain_en: It is named after the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps landing at Gallipoli on 25 April 1915.
questions.explain_vi: Anzac tưởng nhớ mọi người Úc phục vụ và hy sinh trong chiến tranh, xung đột và gìn giữ hòa bình.

questions.question: Which statement about national symbols is correct?

options.text: The national colours are the same as the flag colours (blue, white and red)
National colours are green and gold; the flag is blue, white and red
The national flower is the waratah

questions.explain_en: Sports uniforms are usually green and gold. This is a frequent exam trap.
questions.explain_vi: Bẫy hay gặp: màu quốc gia xanh lá-vàng, khác màu cờ xanh-trắng-đỏ.

questions.question: Freedom of speech means you may campaign to change laws:

options.text: Even if you break other Australian laws while doing so
So long as at all times you are still obeying Australian laws
Only if the Prime Minister agrees in writing

questions.explain_en: You must also respect other people’s freedom of speech and expression.
questions.explain_vi: Được vận động đổi luật miễn là luôn tuân thủ pháp luật Úc.

questions.question: Which is listed as a responsibility, not merely a privilege?

options.text: Serve on a jury if called to do so

questions.explain_en: Passport, standing for parliament and consular help are privileges. Jury service is a responsibility.
questions.explain_vi: Bồi thẩm đoàn là nghĩa vụ. Hộ chiếu và tranh cử là quyền lợi.

questions.question: ‘Fair go’ is described as ensuring:

options.text: Formal class distinctions in Australian society
There are no formal class distinctions - success from talent, work and effort, not wealth or background
Jobs go to the richest applicant

questions.explain_en: Equal opportunity is a core equality in Part 2 and is repeated as a value in Part 4.
questions.explain_vi: Fair go: không phân biệt giai cấp chính thức; thành quả nhờ tài năng và nỗ lực.

questions.question: In the 1967 Referendum, more than 90 per cent of Australians voted Yes to:

options.text: Allow Aboriginal peoples to be counted in the Census

questions.explain_en: This is the book’s example of changing the Constitution by referendum.
questions.explain_vi: Trưng cầu 1967: hơn 90% đồng ý để thổ dân bản địa được tính vào điều tra dân số.

questions.question: Why does the Constitution divide power between legislative, executive and judicial branches?

options.text: To give the police all the power
To stop one person, or one group, from holding all the power
To copy the United Nations exactly

questions.explain_en: These three powers are written into the Australian Constitution.
questions.explain_vi: Tam quyền phân lập để không một người hay nhóm nào nắm hết quyền.

questions.question: Which list of leaders is correctly matched?

options.text: Premier = territory; Chief Minister = state; Mayor = Australia
Premier = state government; Chief Minister = territory government; Mayor or Shire President = local government
Premier = federal government; Prime Minister = a city

questions.explain_en: Learn the title table in Part 3. Mixing Premier and Chief Minister is a common error.
questions.explain_vi: Thủ hiến = tiểu bang; Chief Minister = lãnh thổ; Thị trưởng = địa phương.

questions.question: How many senators do the ACT and the Northern Territory elect in total?
questions.explain_en: Each territory elects two senators. Each state elects 12.
questions.explain_vi: ACT và NT mỗi nơi bầu 2 thượng nghị sĩ (tổng 4).

questions.question: Domestic and family violence can include:

options.text: Hitting, isolating a family member from friends and family, or threatening children or pets
Disagreements about which school to choose

questions.explain_en: It is behaviour or threats that aim to control a partner by causing fear or threatening their safety.
questions.explain_vi: Gồm đánh đập, cô lập khỏi bạn bè/gia đình, hoặc đe dọa con cái hay thú nuôi.

questions.question: Road and traffic rules are controlled by:
questions.explain_en: People can be fined or sent to prison for breaking traffic laws.
questions.explain_vi: Luật giao thông do chính phủ tiểu bang và lãnh thổ kiểm soát.

questions.question: Independents in parliament are:

options.text: People who do not belong to any political party

questions.explain_en: Most parliamentarians belong to parties (Liberal, Labor, Nationals, Greens). Some are independents.
questions.explain_vi: Nghị sĩ độc lập không thuộc đảng nào.

questions.question: You should follow the law:

options.text: Even if no one is watching, otherwise you will face penalties

questions.explain_en: Under the Rule of Law everybody should obey the law and not break it at any time.
questions.explain_vi: Phải tuân luật cả khi không ai theo dõi.

questions.question: A protest that injures people or damages property:

options.text: Is still protected as freedom of association
Is allowed on Australia Day only

questions.explain_en: All protests must be peaceful and must not injure any person or damage property.
questions.explain_vi: Biểu tình gây thương tích hoặc phá tài sản là trái luật.

questions.question: Stalking a person online, or making racially abusive comments about a person online:

options.text: Can be illegal - many forms of cyber abuse are illegal in Australia

questions.explain_en: Online abuse is not accepted. Report it to police and the platform.
questions.explain_vi: Nhiều hình thức bạo lực trên mạng, gồm stalking và bình luận phân biệt chủng tộc, là bất hợp pháp.

questions.question: Which statement about dual citizenship is correct?

options.text: It may be allowed, but an Australian citizen in Australia must follow all Australian laws at all times
It lets you ignore Australian law inside Australia

questions.explain_en: Dual citizenship is allowed if the other country allows it. It does not override Australian law, and it blocks standing for parliament.
questions.explain_vi: Quốc tịch kép được phép nếu nước kia cho phép; ở Úc vẫn phải theo luật Úc.

questions.question: Volunteering is described as:

options.text: A way to avoid paying tax
A great opportunity to share knowledge, learn skills, and increase belonging to the community

questions.explain_en: Australia has a strong tradition of community service and volunteering in the spirit of mateship.
questions.explain_vi: Tình nguyện giúp chia sẻ kiến thức, học kỹ năng và hòa nhập cộng đồng.

questions.question: People from how many countries have made Australia their home, according to the book?
questions.explain_en: Australia combines ethnic and cultural diversity with national unity. Citizenship is the common bond.
questions.explain_vi: Người từ hơn 200 quốc gia đã chọn Úc làm nhà.

questions.question: Queensland is:

options.text: The second-largest state, with the Great Barrier Reef along its eastern coast
An island south of Bass Strait

questions.explain_en: Capital Brisbane. Torres Strait Islands lie to the north.
questions.explain_vi: Queensland là tiểu bang lớn thứ hai; Great Barrier Reef dọc bờ đông.

questions.question: South Australia’s capital and noted features include:

options.text: Adelaide, fine colonial architecture, the Barossa Valley and the Flinders Ranges
Hobart, Port Arthur and Cradle Mountain

questions.explain_en: Match capitals and icons; do not mix WA, SA and Tasmania.
questions.explain_vi: Nam Úc: Adelaide, kiến trúc thuộc địa, Barossa, Flinders Ranges.

questions.question: The yellow circle on the Australian Aboriginal Flag represents:
questions.explain_en: Black = peoples, red = earth, yellow circle = sun.
questions.explain_vi: Vòng tròn vàng trên cờ thổ dân bản địa tượng trưng mặt trời.

questions.question: At a citizenship ceremony, you do not become an Australian citizen until you:
questions.explain_en: You may choose whether to say ‘under God’. A holy book is optional.
questions.explain_vi: Bạn chưa là công dân cho đến khi đọc lời tuyên thệ. Có thể bỏ ‘có Thượng Đế chứng giám’.

questions.question: Which statement about religious holidays and government is true?

options.text: Christian public holidays mean Christianity is the official national religion
There are Christian public holidays, but Australia has no official national religion and the government is secular

questions.explain_en: Heritage and holidays are not the same as an official state religion.
questions.explain_vi: Có ngày lễ Cơ đốc nhưng Úc không có quốc giáo; chính phủ thế tục.

questions.question: If you are not correctly enrolled:

options.text: You can still vote if you bring your passport
You are not able to vote in an election
The AEC will vote for you

questions.explain_en: Citizens 18+ must enrol to vote in federal, state and territory elections and constitutional referendums.
questions.explain_vi: Không ghi danh đúng thì không bỏ phiếu được.

questions.question: Which is a privilege of citizenship related to children?

options.text: Children born overseas can never become Australian
Citizens can apply for their child born overseas to become an Australian citizen by descent
Only sons may become citizens by descent

questions.explain_en: This is listed under privileges in Part 2.
questions.explain_vi: Quyền lợi: đăng ký quốc tịch theo huyết thống cho con sinh ở nước ngoài.

questions.question: Who represents the King in each Australian state?

options.text: A Governor, in a role similar to the Governor-General

questions.explain_en: The King appoints the Governor-General on the PM’s advice. State Governors represent the King in each state.
questions.explain_vi: Mỗi tiểu bang có Toàn quyền đại diện Quốc vương, vai trò tương tự Tổng Toàn quyền.

questions.question: The Governor-General’s reserve powers:

options.text: Are used every sitting day of parliament
Can only be used in specific circumstances
Let the Governor-General write all tax laws alone

questions.explain_en: Everyday roles include Royal Assent, ceremonial duties, approving appointments, starting a federal election, and Commander-in-Chief.
questions.explain_vi: Quyền bảo lưu chỉ dùng trong hoàn cảnh được ấn định.

questions.question: Which services are primarily state and territory responsibilities?

options.text: Hospitals and health services, schools, police and ambulance, public transport

questions.explain_en: Some responsibilities can overlap, but this is the book’s primary split.
questions.explain_vi: Y tế, trường học, cảnh sát, xe cứu thương, giao thông công cộng chủ yếu thuộc tiểu bang/lãnh thổ.

questions.question: People are free to join a political party in Australia:

options.text: If they choose - joining is a freedom, not a requirement
Only if they were born in Australia

questions.explain_en: Main parties named: Liberal, Labor, Nationals, Australian Greens.
questions.explain_vi: Được tự do vào đảng nếu muốn - không bắt buộc.

questions.question: The High Court of Australia:

options.text: Has the ultimate power to apply and interpret the laws of Australia

questions.explain_en: The Constitution established Parliament and the High Court.
questions.explain_vi: Tòa án Tối cao có quyền tối cao áp dụng và diễn giải luật Úc.

questions.question: Which is an example of executive power?

options.text: The Prime Minister, ministers and the Governor-General putting laws into practice

questions.explain_en: Ministers are responsible for government departments.
questions.explain_vi: Hành pháp: Thủ tướng, bộ trưởng và Tổng Toàn quyền thi hành luật.

questions.question: You can raise concerns about government policy by:
