questions.explain_en: If you tell your representative a law needs to change, they should consider the suggestion.
questions.explain_vi: Liên hệ dân biểu đã bầu để nêu quan ngại về chính sách.

questions.question: Which result would FAIL the official citizenship test?

options.text: 16/20 overall but only 4/5 values questions correct

questions.explain_en: You must get all five values questions right AND at least 15/20. One values miss fails the test.
questions.explain_vi: 16/20 nhưng sai 1 câu giá trị vẫn TRƯỢT. Phải đúng 5/5 giá trị VÀ đạt 15/20.

questions.question: Class distinction in the Australian ‘fair go’ sense:

options.text: Is a formal part of society
Should not limit people - everyone should have equal opportunity to succeed
Means jobs go to the nobility

questions.explain_en: People should not be limited by any kind of class distinction.
questions.explain_vi: Không bị giới hạn bởi phân biệt giai tầng; mọi người có cơ hội như nhau.

questions.question: Creating or sharing racially offensive material on the internet:

options.text: Is a form of racism, which has no place in Australia
Is always legal as freedom of speech
Is required to sit the test

questions.explain_en: Racism includes online material and racially abusive comments in public or at sport.
questions.explain_vi: Tạo hoặc chia sẻ tài liệu xúc phạm chủng tộc trên mạng là phân biệt chủng tộc - không có chỗ ở Úc.

questions.question: Which practice is against Australian law even if a culture or religion allows it?

options.text: Polygamy (being married to more than one person at the same time)

questions.explain_en: Religious practices must not break Australian laws. Australian law must be followed even where it differs from religious laws.
questions.explain_vi: Đa thê trái luật Úc dù tập tục tôn giáo cho phép.

questions.question: Loyalty to Australia in the pledge means:

options.text: You must give up every other citizenship immediately, in all cases
You pledge loyalty to Australia and its people; you still follow Australian law even if you also hold another citizenship
You may undermine Australia’s security if you live overseas

questions.explain_en: The pledge is loyalty to Australia and its people, sharing democratic beliefs, respecting rights and liberties, and upholding the laws.
questions.explain_vi: Tuyên thệ trung thành với nước Úc và người Úc; có quốc tịch khác vẫn phải tuân luật Úc.

questions.question: Which statement about Aboriginal arrival in Australia is correct?

options.text: Archaeology points to 65,000-40,000 years ago; Aboriginal peoples believe creation stories begin with the beginning of time
Only Torres Strait Islander peoples lived on the mainland

questions.explain_en: Both the archaeological timeframe and the creation-story belief are stated in Our Common Bond.
questions.explain_vi: Cả mốc khảo cổ và niềm tin creation stories đều có trong Our Common Bond.

questions.question: Uniting the colonies into one nation helped solve problems such as:

options.text: Expensive trade and transport between colonies, weak defence, and difficulty enforcing law across borders

questions.explain_en: Separate colonies created difficulties with trade, transport, law enforcement and defence.
questions.explain_vi: Các thuộc địa riêng gây khó khăn về thương mại, giao thông, thực thi luật và quốc phòng.

questions.question: On the Commonwealth Coat of Arms, the shield in the centre represents:
questions.explain_en: The shield represents the six states and federation.
questions.explain_vi: Khiên tượng trưng sáu tiểu bang và liên bang.

questions.question: Which statement about Welcome to Country is correct?

options.text: It is performed by an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander custodian of the local region
Only the Prime Minister may perform it

questions.explain_en: A Welcome to Country is performed by a custodian of the local region.
questions.explain_vi: Welcome to Country do người gìn giữ vùng đất đó thực hiện.

questions.question: New South Wales was:

options.text: The first colony established by the British
Separated from the mainland by Bass Strait

questions.explain_en: New South Wales was the first British colony; Sydney is its capital and Australia’s largest city.
questions.explain_vi: NSW là thuộc địa Anh đầu tiên.

questions.question: Respect for all individuals in Australia covers attributes such as:

options.text: Race, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, religion and more

questions.explain_en: Australians are expected to treat each other with dignity regardless of background attributes listed in the book.
questions.explain_vi: Tôn trọng gồm nhiều yếu tố như chủng tộc, giới tính, tôn giáo và hơn thế.

questions.question: Which statement about Christian public holidays and religion in Australia is correct?

options.text: Christian public holidays mean Christianity is the official national religion
There are Christian public holidays, but Australia has no official national religion and the government is secular
Religious law overrides Australian law on holidays

questions.explain_en: Judaeo-Christian heritage and Christian holidays exist alongside a secular government with no official national religion.
questions.explain_vi: Có ngày nghỉ Kitô giáo nhưng không có quốc giáo; chính phủ thế tục.

questions.question: Which of these is a Governor-General role?

options.text: Commander-in-Chief of the Australian Defence Force

questions.explain_en: Roles include Royal Assent, ceremonial duties, approving appointments, starting a federal election, and Commander-in-Chief.
questions.explain_vi: Toàn quyền là Tổng tư lệnh Lực lượng Quốc phòng Úc, cùng các vai trò khác.

questions.question: The Governor-General’s reserve powers:

options.text: Can only be used in specific circumstances
Allow the Governor-General to write all tax laws alone

questions.explain_en: Reserve powers can only be used in specific circumstances.
questions.explain_vi: Quyền dự trữ chỉ dùng trong hoàn cảnh đặc biệt.

questions.question: How is the Australian Government generally formed after a federal election?

options.text: By the party or coalition with the majority of members in the House of Representatives
By the party with the most mayors

questions.explain_en: The majority party or coalition in the House of Representatives forms government; its leader becomes Prime Minister.
questions.explain_vi: Đảng/liên minh đa số ở Hạ viện thành lập chính phủ.

questions.question: Main political parties in Australia include:

options.text: The Liberal Party, Australian Labor Party, the Nationals and the Australian Greens

questions.explain_en: Those are the main political parties named in Our Common Bond. Independents belong to no party.
questions.explain_vi: Các đảng chính gồm Liberal, Labor, Nationals và Greens.

questions.question: Which statement about states and territories is correct?

options.text: States have rights recognised by the Constitution; territory laws can be altered or revoked by the Australian Government
Territories have stronger constitutional rights than states
ACT elects 12 senators like a state

questions.explain_en: States have constitutional rights; territories do not. ACT and NT each elect two senators.
questions.explain_vi: Tiểu bang có quyền theo Hiến pháp; lãnh thổ thì không.

questions.question: A magistrate in Australia is:

options.text: A judge of a lower court

questions.explain_en: A magistrate is a judge of a lower court.
questions.explain_vi: Magistrate là thẩm phán của tòa cấp thấp hơn.

questions.question: If you break an Australian law you did not know about:

options.text: You could still be charged; not knowing the law is no excuse

questions.explain_en: Not knowing the law is no excuse.
questions.explain_vi: Không biết luật không phải lý do miễn tội.

questions.question: Federal government responsibilities include:

options.text: Immigration, citizenship, defence, foreign affairs and taxation

questions.explain_en: Those are examples of Australian Government responsibilities in the book.
questions.explain_vi: Liên bang phụ trách nhập cư, quốc tịch, quốc phòng, đối ngoại và thuế.

questions.question: Under Australian values, promoting violence against a group because of culture or religion is:

options.text: Never acceptable and against Australian values and law

questions.explain_en: It is never acceptable to promote violence against another person or group.
questions.explain_vi: Không bao giờ được kích động bạo lực vì văn hóa hay tôn giáo.

questions.question: Forced marriage in Australia is:

options.text: A cultural choice protected by religious law
A crime that can result in severe legal penalties

questions.explain_en: Forced marriage is against the law and can result in imprisonment.
questions.explain_vi: Cưỡng hôn là tội, có thể bị phạt nặng.

questions.question: Dual citizenship means:

options.text: Australian law does not apply in Australia
You may hold another citizenship if that country’s laws allow, but must follow Australian laws in Australia

questions.explain_en: Dual citizenship is allowed, but Australian law still applies in Australia.
questions.explain_vi: Quốc tịch kép được phép nhưng luật Úc vẫn áp dụng khi ở Úc.

questions.question: Using social media to share official government secrets would:
questions.explain_en: Australian society is based on shared obligations not to undermine Australia’s interests and security.
questions.explain_vi: Chia sẻ bí mật chính phủ làm hại lợi ích và an ninh Úc.

questions.question: Incidents of racism can also be reported to:
questions.explain_en: Racism complaints can be made to the Australian Human Rights Commission.
questions.explain_vi: Có thể khiếu nại phân biệt chủng tộc tới Australian Human Rights Commission.

questions.question: Queensland is:

options.text: The second largest state; Torres Strait Islands lie to its north
Separated from the mainland by Bass Strait

questions.explain_en: Queensland is the second largest state; Torres Strait Islands lie to the north.
questions.explain_vi: Queensland lớn thứ hai; Torres Strait ở phía bắc.

questions.question: National institutions in Canberra include:

options.text: Parliament House and the High Court of Australia

questions.explain_en: Parliament House and the High Court are located in Canberra.
questions.explain_vi: Parliament House và High Court nằm ở Canberra.

questions.question: An Acknowledgement of Country:

options.text: Can only be given by a Traditional Custodian
Can be given by anyone and pays respect to Traditional Custodians and Elders past and present

questions.explain_en: Anyone can deliver an Acknowledgement of Country.
questions.explain_vi: Ai cũng có thể nói Acknowledgement of Country.

questions.question: Anzac Day remembers:

options.text: The sacrifice of Australians who served and died in wars, conflicts and peacekeeping, and honours all servicemen and women

questions.explain_en: Anzac Day is a solemn day remembering service and sacrifice.
questions.explain_vi: Anzac tưởng nhớ người phục vụ và hy sinh trong chiến tranh, xung đột và gìn giữ hòa bình.

questions.question: Equality of opportunity and a ‘fair go’ means:

options.text: What someone achieves should result from talents, work and effort rather than wealth or background
Jobs must be reserved by family name

questions.explain_en: A fair go aims to ensure there are no formal class distinctions.
questions.explain_vi: Fair go: thành quả từ tài năng và nỗ lực, không phải gia thế.

questions.question: Which is both a responsibility and a privilege of Australian citizenship?

options.text: Voting in federal and state or territory elections and in a referendum

questions.explain_en: Voting is listed as both a responsibility and a privilege for citizens aged 18 or over.
questions.explain_vi: Đi bầu vừa là nghĩa vụ vừa là quyền lợi.

questions.question: Executive power in Australia is the power to:

options.text: Make all local parking signs only

questions.explain_en: Executive power puts laws into practice; it includes the Prime Minister, ministers and the Governor-General.
questions.explain_vi: Quyền hành pháp là thi hành luật.

questions.question: Judicial power belongs to:

options.text: Courts and judges, independent of parliament and government

questions.explain_en: Judges interpret and apply the law; courts are independent.
questions.explain_vi: Quyền tư pháp thuộc tòa án và thẩm phán, độc lập với quốc hội và chính phủ.

questions.question: People who do not belong to any political party are called:
questions.explain_en: Parliamentarians who do not belong to any party are called independents.
questions.explain_vi: Nghị sĩ không thuộc đảng gọi là independent.

questions.question: Local government responsibilities include:

options.text: Rubbish collection, parks, local roads, street signs and building permits

questions.explain_en: Local councils deliver local services such as rubbish, parks, roads and building permits.
questions.explain_vi: Hội đồng địa phương lo rác, công viên, đường phố và giấy phép xây dựng.

questions.question: Which list matches the titles correctly?

options.text: Premier = state; Chief Minister = territory; Mayor or Shire President = local
Premier = territory; Chief Minister = state; Mayor = Australia

questions.explain_en: Premier leads a state; Chief Minister a territory; Mayor/Shire President a local government.
questions.explain_vi: Premier = tiểu bang; Chief Minister = lãnh thổ; Mayor = địa phương.

questions.question: Which traffic behaviour is illegal in Australia according to the book?

options.text: Using a hand-held mobile device while driving

questions.explain_en: It is against the law to use a hand-held mobile device while driving.
questions.explain_vi: Dùng điện thoại cầm tay khi lái xe là bất hợp pháp.

questions.question: The Australian Federal Police is responsible for:

options.text: Crimes against federal laws (for example drug trafficking and national security) and general police work in the ACT

questions.explain_en: The AFP investigates federal crimes and does general policing in the ACT.
questions.explain_vi: AFP xử lý tội liên bang và cảnh sát thường ở ACT.

questions.question: How can the Australian Constitution be changed?

options.text: By a referendum with a double majority
By a local council vote only

questions.explain_en: A double majority means a national majority and a majority of voters in a majority of states.
questions.explain_vi: Đổi Hiến pháp cần trưng cầu dân ý với đa số kép.

questions.question: When both Houses agree to a Bill, it becomes law after:
questions.explain_en: The Governor-General signs the Bill (Royal Assent) so it becomes law.
questions.explain_vi: Toàn quyền ký Royal Assent để dự luật thành luật.

questions.question: The age of consent in Australia is:

options.text: 16 or 17 depending on the state or territory; 15 is illegal everywhere

questions.explain_en: Age of consent is 16 or 17 by state/territory; 15 is illegal in all states and territories.
questions.explain_vi: Tuổi đồng ý là 16 hoặc 17; 15 bất hợp pháp mọi nơi.

questions.question: Same-sex marriage in Australia is:

options.text: Legal; two people can marry each other, including two men or two women

questions.explain_en: Under Australian law, two people can marry each other, including two men or two women.
questions.explain_vi: Hôn nhân đồng giới hợp pháp ở Úc.

questions.question: Australians believe change should occur through:

options.text: Discussion, peaceful persuasion and the democratic process

questions.explain_en: Australians reject violence as a way to change a person’s mind or the law.
questions.explain_vi: Thay đổi qua bàn thảo, thuyết phục ôn hòa và quy trình dân chủ.

questions.question: In Australia, a better-qualified woman:

options.text: Cannot get a job ahead of a man
Has the right to get a job ahead of a man

questions.explain_en: It is a right for a woman to get a job ahead of a man if she has better qualifications and skills.
questions.explain_vi: Nam nữ bình đẳng khi tuyển dụng.

questions.question: Some Australian laws, such as those about sexual activity with a child under 16:

options.text: Apply to Australian citizens even when overseas
Do not apply to dual citizens

questions.explain_en: Some Australian laws must also be followed by Australian citizens overseas.
questions.explain_vi: Một số luật Úc vẫn áp dụng khi công dân ở nước ngoài.
